full_judgment: 18. The fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence is that the prosecution is required to give satisfactory proof of corpus delicti i.e.a crime has been committed that is to say, that the man is dead and that his death has been caused by a crime. It is true that in law a conviction for an offence does not necessarily depend upon corpus delecti being found. There may b reliable evidence of the commission of the murder though the corpus delicti not traceable The prosecution has to prove that the accused is the person who murdered the deceased and no one else. The general presumption is that the, accused is innocent unless the contrary is proved and in general, the more the serious di, crime the more clearly must it be proved. There, is another presumption that every man is to be resumed to have intended the natural and probable consequences of his acts.
